nodes.question: How much manure is applied to the spring barley in rotation 1 per hectare?
nodes.answer: 27.7 Mg ha 1 of manure is applied to the spring barley in rotation 1.
nodes.paragraph: The cover crops were a mixture of clover and ryegrass. The other 500 hectares included grass-clover grazing, grass clover silage production, and pea-spring barley for silage (rotation 2). This area was considered out- side of the system boundary as it was assumed not to be affected by the actions in rotation 1. The manure production of the 560 cattle was 18,0 Mg fresh matter (FM) year 1, with 49.1 g N kg 1 dry matter (DM) (Fontaine et al. 2020b). Assuming 189 grazing days (6 h day 1), 15,600 Mg are collected in the animal house and stored to be field applied. This results in 27.7 Mg ha 1 applied to the spring barley in rotation 1. Of the barley produced, 1,344 Mg grains are used for feed, and 336 Mg straw is needed for feed and bedding. Any additional barley grain production was assumed to be sold and is modelled to substitute other organic barley production at the market, using data from the Ecoin- vent database (Wernet et al. 2016).

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How many grains were sown in each pot during the experiment?
nodes.answer: Ten grains were sown in each pot.
nodes.paragraph: In each stage, abnormalities were counted and expressed as a proportion of dividing cells. Simulated drought experiment and plant growth attributes Grains were planted in 10 pots replica, each pot (25 cm in diameter and 25 cm in depth) containing 3.5 kg of homogeneous loamy clay soil. Ten grains were sown in each pot. Pots were divided into two groups of treat - ments. The first treatments were exposed to seven doses of gamma irradiation and irrigated by distilled water, and the second treatments was exposed to the same doses of radiation accompanied with simulated drought stress imposed by 10% of polyethylene glycol (PEG). Grains of control were not exposed to any treatment. After 21 days of planting, morphological parameters were evaluated for 10 plants randomly selected for each treatment. These parameters are root length, root fresh weight and root dry weight, shoot length, shoot diameter, fresh and dry weight of shoot, number of leaves and leaf surface area. Morphological parameters were assessed accord - ing to the International Seed Testing Association (ISTA) rules [29].

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What did Hooper et al. (2012) report about yields in short and simplified crop rotations?
nodes.answer: Hooper et al. (2012) reported a yield reduction of 5 to 10% in response to a 21 to 40% decrease in crop species.
nodes.paragraph: Yields often show a declining trend in short and simplified crop rotations, as reported by Hooper et al. (2012), who found a yield reduction of 5 10% in response to a 21 40% decrease in crop species. Diversification of cropping systems has proven effective in reversing this declining trend (Bennett et al. 2012). Yields tend to increase with greater diversity, although the posi- tive effect might not always be significant (Archer et al. 2020).
